traps: Swapping the values and stating x = 9.2 rupees and y = 13.2 rupees
Giving integer approximations such as x = 13 rupees and y = 9 rupees without justification
Providing only one of the two equations or omitting the second equation
Solving the system incorrectly and obtaining values like x = 10 rupees, y = 12 rupees
Stating the answer as a relationship (e.g., x = y + 4) without giving the numeric values

checks.ask: Does the answer correctly set up the two simultaneous equations 15x + 10y = 290 and 12x + 18y = 324?
Does the answer give the value of x (cost of an apple) as 13.2 rupees?
Does the answer give the value of y (cost of an orange) as 9.2 rupees?
